questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

To change (A)/ one's name now, (B)/ he will need to have their (C)/ birth registered in the state. (D)
questions.s:
Part C has an error.

In the given sentence, 'one' is an indefinite pronoun. If 'one' is used in a sentence to refer to 'people in general', the same pronoun should be used throughout the sentence. So, the pronoun 'he' should be replaced with 'one' to rectify the given sentence.

The correct sentence is: To change one's name now, one will need to have their birth registered in the state.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q:
In this novel, I came across some words which meaning I did not know.

[СРО-12/3/2019 S1]
questions.s:
In the sentence, we need to use "whose" instead of "which". This is because "whose" shows possession or belonging. We're talking about the meaning of the words, so we use "whose" to show that the meaning belongs to the words.

Correct sentence: In this novel, I came across some words whose meaning I did not know.

"Whose" is used to show that the meaning belongs to the words.

"Which" is used for things, not for showing possession.

questions.s:
Correct Answer: who I found

"who" is incorrect because it refers to people. For non-living things like "album," we should use "which" or "that."

Correct sentence: This is the album which I found in the garage.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select option ‘No substitution required’.

Often it makes one wonder at the sights you see.
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'one sees'.

Key Points

  • The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'one sees' should be used instead of 'you see'.
  • ‘One’ means any person, but not any particular person.
  • However, when we use ‘one’ in a sentence we always use ‘one’ as a pronoun not pronouns like you, him, he, etc.
  • Moreover, ‘one’ is a singular subject so it will take ‘sees’ as a singular verb.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct Sentence: Often it makes one wonder at the sights one sees.

questions.q:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

To who (1)/did you (2)/speak last night? (3)/No error (4)
questions.s:
Here the correct answer is 1.
Key Points:-

  • In the above given sentence, the error is in part 1.
  • It is so because instead of 'who' here we will just use 'whom'.
  • One easy way to find out what to use is that If the question can be answered with 'he/she', the question must be asked with 'who'.
  • But if the answer involves 'him/her', question must be asked with 'whom'. 
  • Here we can't say 'I was speaking with he'.
  • Rather 'I was speaking with him' is correct.
  • Therefore, 'who' will be replaced by 'whom'.

Thus, the correct sentence is To whom did you speak last night.

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Every soldier and every officer was in their place.
questions.s:
The erroneous part is their place i.e. this part has an error.

Key Points

  • Replace 'their' with 'his'.
  • When two singular nouns joined by and are preceded by each or every, the pronoun must be singular in number.
    • Every soldier and every sailor was in his place.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 3.
     
The correct sentence: Every soldier and every officer was in his place.
Additional Information
  • A personal pronoun referring back to a collective noun must be in the singular number if the collective noun is viewed as a whole.
    • The jury has given its verdict.
    • The fleet will reach its destination in a week.
  • If the focus is on the individual members of the group, the pronoun should be in the plural number.
    • The jury were divided in their opinion.
